chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from Ali (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who confessed before his death to So-and-so and So-and-so, that one of them had a thousand dirhams with him, then he died in that state, Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'Whichever of them produces evidence, to him belongs the wealth; and if neither of them produces evidence, the wealth is divided between them as two halves.'

key_terms.عِنْدَ مَوْتِهِ: At the time of death / in the final illness

ai.seo_question: How is a debt divided when the deceased confessed to two people but didn't specify who was owed the money?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, transmitted through Ali ibn Abi Talib, establishes the principle of *al-ikrar* (confession) in *al-marad* (deathbed illness) within Shia jurisprudence. It clarifies that when a debt is acknowledged to multiple parties without specific allocation, the burden of proof (*bayyina*) determines the distribution, ensuring justice by awarding the full amount to the verified claimant or splitting it equally if evidence is lacking for both.
